```{r, include = FALSE}
# The guide downloads data from Zenodo, so its code is shown and not run when the package is built.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This guide loads one version of Toronto Election Results and walks through six uses of it.
Replace the version with the one you cite; `te_versions()` lists them.

```{r}
library(torontoelections)
version <- "results-2026-11-30.1"
```

## 1. Load the candidacies of a pinned version

```{r}
candidacies <- te_candidacies(version = version)
dim(candidacies)
attr(candidacies$incumbent, "description")
```

Each row is one candidate in one Contest. Counts are integers, flags logical and dates `Date`.
A missing value means what the codebook says it means; `te_codebook("candidacies", version)`
lists every column.

## 2. Incumbents' win rates by office

```{r}
incumbents <- candidacies[candidacies$incumbent %in% TRUE & !is.na(candidacies$elected), ]
tapply(incumbents$elected, incumbents$office_type, mean)
```

`incumbent` is `NA` where the release holds no roster that settles it, so keep the rows where it
is `TRUE` rather than treating `NA` as `FALSE`.

## 3. One person's career across levels of government

```{r}
people <- te_people(version = version)
person <- people$person_id[people$preferred_name == "Olivia Chow"]
career <- te_careers(person, version = version)
career[, c("election_date", "office_type", "district_name", "party_name", "votes", "elected")]
```

`te_careers()` accepts a retired Person ID too, and follows it to the Person that replaced it.

## 4. Join People to Wikidata and ParlInfo

```{r}
members <- people[!is.na(people$wikidata_id), ]
head(members[, c("person_id", "preferred_name", "wikidata_id", "parlinfo_id")])
```

Only People who sat in the House of Commons or the Legislative Assembly of Ontario have these IDs.

## 5. Check that a result does not rest on structural links

```{r}
confirmed <- te_candidacies(version = version, source_confirmed_only = TRUE)
repeat_runners <- function(frame) sum(table(frame$person_id) > 1)
c(all_links = repeat_runners(candidacies), source_confirmed = repeat_runners(confirmed))
```

With `source_confirmed_only = TRUE`, a Candidacy whose link rests only on the build's structural
rules has no Person. Repeating an analysis this way shows how much it depends on those links.

## 6. Map the 2022 council results

```{r}
shapes <- te_districts(version = version, geometry = TRUE)  # needs sf
winners <- candidacies[candidacies$office_type == "councillor" &
                         candidacies$election_year == 2022 &
                         candidacies$elected %in% TRUE, c("district_id", "vote_share")]
winners_map <- merge(shapes, winners, by = "district_id")
plot(winners_map["vote_share"])
```

Districts in different boundary sets cover different areas, so map one election, or one boundary
set, at a time.
